missionPremise: OPS-16 amendment A-020. Six of fourteen rails carry zero rows in county_facet_coverage and are therefore permanently not-yet on the console regardless of the store. This lane writes the MEASUREMENT SPEC for each — unit, covered vs established-absence vs not-yet, denominator with its rule — so the scorer capability lane SS-W12 is building has something correct to plug into. The split exists because the last comparable programme built twelve writers and three scorers and nobody wrote down what scoring meant.

premiseVerifiedAtSource.claim: the six rails carry zero cells with a source AND zero with a coverage pct across all 254 counties
premiseVerifiedAtSource.label: VERIFIED by this lane
premiseVerifiedAtSource.instrument: psql against CORTEX_DATABASE_URL: SELECT facet, count(*), count(DISTINCT county_fips), max(checked_at) FROM county_facet_coverage GROUP BY facet ORDER BY facet
premiseVerifiedAtSource.verdict: PREMISE HOLDS. Nine facet values exist and none of the six is among them. The six rails have no ledger row of any kind, so a recompute cannot move them; only a scorer that does not exist can.

theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.trap: reach ceilings are not trustworthy as briefed
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.whatIFound: The rrc-wells ceiling of 1 is not a probe result at all. VERIFIED at source: /p/legacy-design-tools/lib/db/src/railCoverageCapability.ts declares STATIC_RAIL_CAPABILITIES with rrc-wells maxCountiesReachable hardcoded to 1 and reachPct 1/254, citing lib/adapters/src/federal/texas-rrc.ts. That adapter is the RETIRED path.
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.reDerivation: VERIFIED by this lane. The live apply path is packages/engine-core/src/well-fact/fetch-wells-staged.ts, whose header reads 'NEVER use the Harris County ArcGIS mirror for apply — it holds ~0.92% of TX', and write-well-fact-county.mjs REFUSES TO RUN if the source still points at gis.hctx.net. The real source is staged table tx_rrc_well in cortex: 1,396,049 wells, count(DISTINCT county_fips) = 254, plus 1,556 rows with NULL county_fips still reachable by lng/lat bbox. Harris 48201 holds 12,850 of those 1,396,049 — 0.92%, exactly the figure the code comment names and within 0.4% of the standing memory's '12,796 features, extent is one county'. The memory measured the MIRROR. The mirror is not the source.
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.verdict: RE-DERIVED CEILING FOR rrc-wells IS 254, NOT 1. Applying the briefed ceiling would have manufactured 253 false out-of-reach cells. The standing memory 'RRC wells source is HARRIS-ONLY' is true of a retired adapter and false of the live writer; it needs re-adjudication by the operator, not silent carry-forward.

theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.trap: an established absence is not bounded by an acquisition source's reach (mud 209/186)
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.whatIFound: The same shape exists at PARCEL scale and I reproduced it. Crane 48103 holds 5,805 parcel-node atoms: 5,553 with geometryLoaded true and 252 with geometryLoaded false. rrc-pipeline-fact determinations there number 5,567 = all 5,553 geometry-true nodes PLUS 14 of the geometry-false ones. A denominator of 'geometry-true nodes' would score 5,567/5,553 = 100.25%.
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.ruleAdopted: The per-parcel denominator is EVERY parcel-node atom in the county, with the geometryLoaded-false subcount published beside it as a measured exclusion class, never subtracted from it. Determinations are counted only where they JOIN a parcel-node; orphan determinations are counted and reported separately. Under that rule the ratio cannot exceed 100% by construction, and the shortfall is explained rather than hidden.
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.orphanCheckRun: VERIFIED: Bastrop 48021 rrc-pipeline-fact, 62,256 determinations, 0 with no matching parcel-node atom.
theTwoTrapsCheckedNotInherited.incidentalCorrection: SS-W9's close labels 48103 'Callahan'. county_manifest says 48103 = Crane and Callahan = 48059. A naming error that moves no number; SS-W9's 60,396 / 1,839 / 58,557 well figures for 48103 reproduce exactly under my own query.

denominatorRuleEstablished.statement: For every parcel-keyed depth rail the county figure is (determinations joined to a parcel-node) / (parcel-node atoms in the county), and it travels with a second measured figure: (determinations) / (DISTINCT usable prop_id in txgio_parcel for the county), which is the writer-reach number.
denominatorRuleEstablished.whyTwoNumbers: They differ, and the difference is the finding. The writer-reach denominator is the set the depth writers actually iterate; the parcel-node denominator is what a customer's sheet is drawn from. Publishing only the first lets a rail read 100% while spine parcels carry nothing.
denominatorRuleEstablished.usablePropIdPredicate: packages/atoms/src/fact-writer-ids.ts isUsablePropId + normalizeForJoin, expressed in SQL: prop_id non-null, non-blank, not all-zero, and matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ after leading-zero strip.
fiveIndependentExactMatchesVerifiedByThi: 48201 Harris: usable prop_ids 1,523,640 = parcel-node atoms 1,523,640 = rrc-pipeline-fact 1,523,640 = rail-corridor-fact 1,523,640
48103 Crane: usable prop_ids 5,567 = rrc-pipeline-fact 5,567 = well-fact distinct parcels touched 5,567; parcel-node 5,805
48021 Bastrop: usable prop_ids 62,256 = rrc-pipeline-fact 62,256 = rail-corridor-fact 62,256; parcel-node 62,398
denominatorRuleEstablished.rejectedDenominator: county_manifest.parcel_count_est. VERIFIED: it diverges from the parcel-node count by more than 20% in 19 of 253 counties and by 184% on Harris (est 536,512 against 1,523,640 atoms). Statewide sums agree to within 2.7%, which is exactly how a bad per-county denominator hides.

retractedByMeBeforeItShipped.hypothesis: I suspected count(DISTINCT feature_index) in txgio_parcel was unsound, because the primary key is (county_fips, tile_key, feature_index) so feature_index looked per-tile.
retractedByMeBeforeItShipped.test: min/max feature_index per county against max features in any single tile.
retractedByMeBeforeItShipped.result: 48021 max feature_index 63,356 against 2,498 features in the largest tile; 48261 max 537 against 171 in the largest tile. feature_index is a COUNTY-GLOBAL contiguous index 0..N-1, not per-tile.
retractedByMeBeforeItShipped.verdict: HYPOTHESIS RETRACTED. countyGeometryScoreCli.ts's denominator is sound and its Kenedy 2,400-rows-for-538-features multiplier is real (4.46x, matching the standing rural-seam memory). Recorded because a correction carries the same evidentiary standard as the claim it corrects (DEV_PROCESS 3.2a) and this one failed its own test.

perRailSkeletonAtCP1.roads: Unit is the OSM way, NOT the parcel. road-node entity_id is <fips>:road:<osmWayId> and PARCEL_KEYED_PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES explicitly EXCLUDES road-node (packages/atoms/src/property-instances.ts:213).
perRailSkeletonAtCP1.footprint: Unit is the parcel. Present and per-parcel-absence atoms COLLIDE on the same entity_id suffix :footprint:primary and are distinguishable only in the body.
perRailSkeletonAtCP1.easement: Unit is the COUNTY for 252 of 254 counties by construction. The routing table default is one county-coverage absence atom, explicitly 'not millions of per-parcel sentinels'. Hybrid unit.
perRailSkeletonAtCP1.rrc-wells: Unit is the parcel. Absence is a real atom with entity_id suffix :none.
perRailSkeletonAtCP1.rrc-pipelines: Unit is the parcel. There is NO absence atom in the normal path; 'no pipeline near' is encoded as PRESENT with nearPipeline false.
perRailSkeletonAtCP1.rail-corridor: Unit is the parcel. Same present-with-flag-false shape as pipelines.

cannotBeScoredTodayProvisional: roads — the denominator (ways the pinned Geofabrik PBF yields inside the county boundary, post-taxonomy-filter) exists only inside a writer run and is persisted NOWHERE. VERIFIED: write-road-node-county.mjs computes waysRead into an optional --out summary JSON; cortex pg_tables carries no road table at all, and there is no county-coverage road atom family. Roads can be scored as a binary presence today and as a percentage only after a census is persisted.

footprint — a covered-vs-absent split cannot be read from entity_id. VERIFIED in Wise 48497: :footprint:primary splits 24,629 rows carrying an absence body against 23,799 without, same suffix. An index-only prefix scorer would count all of them as covered.
adversarialReviewOfMyOwnPlan: The brief told me 'rrc-pipelines is bound to an empty atom family while 12.5M of its atoms exist'. I did not relay it. VERIFIED both halves at source: railEngineBinding.ts gives rrc-pipelines atomEntityTypes [] with noWriterReason 'Atom family not registered in engine PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES — no writer until pipeline atom ships', and packages/atoms/src/property-instances.ts line 204 lists 'rrc-pipeline-fact' in PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES. The noWriterReason is false at source. The same binding also gives easement no writer while hauska-engine ships write-utility-easement-county.mjs.
The brief told me utility-easement is the only genuinely empty family. VERIFIED independently: SELECT count(*) WHERE entity_type='utility-easement' returned zero rows in 0.49 seconds.

I am NOT recounting the WRITTEN layer. SS-W9 measured it four hours before this lane started, and the two figures I re-measured (parcel-node per county for 48021/48261/48497, and well-fact Crane 60,396 = 1,839 absence + 58,557 present) reproduce to the atom. The two statewide scans I did attempt (road-node DISTINCT county, atoms GROUP BY entity_type) both exceeded a 300-second statement timeout, which is itself why that audit is a background job and not a checkpoint step.

Risk I am accepting: my spec cannot be validated end-to-end without the scorer SS-W12 is building. Mitigation is that every rule is expressed as a predicate with a test that proves the rule can FIRE on constructed input, so a dead rule is visible before a scorer ever runs.
outOfScopeDeliberately: Building any scorer. That is SS-W12 in legacy-design-tools.
The other eight rails. geometry, cad, zoning, flood, envelope, landuse, owner and mud already carry ledger rows and are not this lane's subject.
Editing railEngineBinding.ts or railCoverageCapability.ts. Both are legacy-design-tools files, both are wrong, both are findings for the planner, neither is mine to edit.
Re-adjudicating the standing RRC-wells memory. I supply the evidence; the ruling is the operator's.
constraintsHonored: Read-only on both production databases. No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or DDL. No atoms bulk-writer slot, no lease, no --apply.
Heavy scans serialized, never parallel. Two exceeded the statement timeout and were abandoned rather than retried wider.
Every query carried an explicit statement_timeout as a connection startup parameter (PGOPTIONS), never as a separate -c statement — SS-W9's F11 records that the separate form silently never applies.
No file touched in packages/retrieval/src/statewide-audit/, packages/retrieval/scripts/, artifacts/three-layer-audit/, .gitignore or pnpm-lock.yaml — the paths SS-W9's open PR #348 holds.
Nothing merged, nothing deployed, nothing pushed to main.
